text:
A nursing pillow, nipple cream and a pumping bra!!!! 

There is nothing worse than having to pump in the hospital because your milk hasn't come in yet or because you have painful breast from over supply and than having to hold the flanges for 20 minutes while you cant even look at your phone or have a drink or snack. 

I have literally bought my friend a pumping bra overnight and brought it to her in the hospital because her milk didnt come in and she was pumping and holding the flanges. Because I wished somebody would have done that for me when I was in the hospital with pre eclampsia after birth and major over supply and a baby that wouldnt latch and I would sit there crying while holding the flanges every 3 hours for 5 days. So yeah bring a pumping/nursing bra. My favorite for the hospital is the Momcozy Hands Free Pumping & Nursing Bra, Adjustable Cotton Breast Pump Bra. Because its cotton and easy.

Unless you’re on pelvic rest or something like that, there’s 0 reason to worry. I carried my 30lbs toddler home from the park 5 days before my 2nd baby was born. Also went crazy nesting the final month and moved all the furniture to vacuum, along with never being patient enough to wait for my husband to bring things up from/down to the basement.

I did utilize a belly band more in my second pregnancy and that helped a lot with back pain.

The few weeks after my c-section were a little tricky, but we knew it was coming so we got toddler comfortable using a small step stool to climb into her crib. There was one time that she woke up early from her nap and I had to just sit next to the crib and talk to her while I waited for my husband to get back from the store. But overall it was relatively uneventful.
Just saw another comment about a birthing/exercise ball - yes!!! Momcozy makes a pink one and a blue one that come with a little inflatable ring so she can bounce without fearing losing her balance.
I have tried a belly band and I'm not sure if it's just the one I have or what but it's uncomfy and feels like I'm squeezing my baby haha. I do have a yoga ball but haven't blown it up yet

title: Reminder to wear your belly band even if you don’t think you need it yet!
text:
I’m 20 weeks and haven‘t stopped working out since I found out I was pregnant. I do modified kickboxing 3 times a week and runs every now and again. I got my belly band two months ago but kept looking at it like, “I don’t need you yet” since I really wasn’t showing.

  
Well, the strain on my pelvis and hips has been creeping up and I didn’t really notice it. My Monday workout TOOK me out and I had so much pelvic pain I couldn’t sleep. Strapped my belly band on for class this evening and holy cow, what a difference. I’m still wearing it right now because the weight off my pelvis and lower back is incredible. 

  
Wish I had started wearing it a month ago!

title: Diastasis recti pain?
text:
First- I have talked with my OB and they ended up ordering PT. So they’re aware of the pain and don’t think it’s anything serious.

Ok I saw some posts about this but they’re all pretty old. Has anyone dealt with pain from their abs separating?? This is the only thing I can think of that’s causing my symptoms.

Week 29 (almost 30), and over maybe a day and a half I developed a tearing/stinging sort of pain over my abdomen- it started down the midline but now has migrated to a spot just left of that. It’s not bad in the morning but even with light activity, it worsens throughout the day and by the end of the day the spot is tender. At that point it hurts to do almost anything- open slightly heavy doors, get out of my car, carry my laptop bag- it all hurts.

I do have a belly band that I was using running (haven’t run since this started), thinking about wearing it all day to see if that helps.

Does anyone else have experience with this? Any ideas for what will help? I can’t imagine how much worse this will get as I get bigger. I’m 4’11” so my belly is big and gonna be huge by the end.

title: Severe pain… this cannot be normal!
text:

title: Didn't think I needed a pregnancy belly band but that Target run humbled me real quick
text:
27 weeks here and honestly didn't think I'd be one of those people asking about pregnancy belly bands. But lol here I am.

The wake-up call was last weekend. I was walking around Target, nothing crazy, just browsing the baby section. Bent down to grab a pack of onesies and literally had to brace myself on the shelf to get back up. My husband was like "you good??" and I'm standing there like... yeah no I'm definitely not good lol.

That's when it hit me: my pelvis feels weirdly heavy, like there's just this constant pressure sitting right on my bladder. It's not painful exactly, but it's... there. And it's starting to mess with normal stuff, getting off the couch, picking things up, even just walking around the grocery store for 20 mins.

I went down the rabbit hole looking up pregnancy belly bands and ngl I didn't expect there to be this many options. Some look like simple stretchy bands, others have all these extra straps and support panels. Kinda overwhelming tbh. And the reviews are all over the place, every brand has people who swear by it and people who say it did absolutely nothing. So now I'm stuck not knowing what's actually worth trying.

If you've used one and it actually helped, I'd love to hear which one worked for you! Really trying to avoid the buy-and-return cycle if I can. TIA!

title: Marathon runner, struggling to run 10k at 16 weeks
text:
I am an experienced runner, and have been running 6-7 days a week for the last 3 years. I found out I was pregnant in June and ran a half PB the same weekend! It may have been adrenaline + fear over not being able to run fast for awhile 😂

Anyways I am 16 weeks now due in early March and running has been SUCH a battle for me. I have to pee once every 3k, I have lower belly cramping and feel like my belly is jostling (that goes away after the first km but it is uncomfortable starting out). I am about 1 minute slower per km. I knew running would be more difficult when pregnant but I don’t think I realized it would become this challenging so early on. 

Any advice for defeated runners? I was supposed to run the Chicago marathon (would’ve been my 5th) in October but decided to defer to next year. Before getting pregnant I was one of those people who swore they would run and stay active the entire time. I do strength train as well and that has been great - I am feeling strong and empowered in the gym. I just find running has the complete opposite effect and makes me feel so gassed and out of shape. Running used to be my happy place and now it is such a grind just to get out there and struggle through it. 

I haven’t tried a belly band yet but open to it. Sorry for venting but I really miss running and I’m genuinely so sad it’s been such a negative thing for me this early on into pregnancy 🫩 any advice?
